text: Why is a MAC address space of 2^48 not enough to make MAC addresses usable globally?
choices: MAC addresses are flat, so no rule summarises a group of them and any device must learn each individually
They are only 48 bits, and IPv6 needs 128
explanation: Flatness, not size, is the problem. Two adjacent MAC addresses may be on opposite sides of the planet, so aggregation is impossible and every forwarding device must know each address individually — which bounds table size and therefore broadcast domain size.
